quotes.text:
Panorama is the working name of Thunderbird's new global message database. All folders and messages
will be stored in a single database, instead of one database per folder as currently happens.

Code for updating the front end's message list is also within scope.

```{warning}
Panorama is under development. It is not live and there are currently no user-facing parts. Feel
free to explore, but you do so at your own risk.

The Panorama code is compiled in when the `MOZ_PANORAMA` compile-time flag is set.
This happens automatically on the nightly channel (i.e. comm-central) only.

`MOZ_PANORAMA` can be used for conditional blocks in C++ code, moz.build files, and other places
where preprocessing happens.

To use Panorama at runtime (instead of the old mork databases), set the pref `mail.panorama.enabled`
to true.

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The initial folder database build was gated directly on NIGHTLY_BUILD. Current mailnews/moz.build uses MOZ_PANORAMA, and the accepted docs describe the separate mail.panorama.enabled runtime preference. The test manifest enables that preference. The documentation labels Panorama as under development and states its goal is a global folder/message database with legacy-interface migration. These are the checked snapshot and documented direction, not a claim that every planned step is complete or every build has Panorama. Static inspection supports this component scope. No runtime test was run for this lesson, and full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion is still pending.
title: Keep Panorama compile-time and runtime activation distinct
